summary: iter36 [SW v4->v5 bump regression] verified end-to-end on preview. (1) Service worker: GET /sw.js returns 200, content-type 'application/javascript; charset=UTF-8', body contains const VERSION = "patchpot-v5" (no v4 references) — activate handler line 21-30 evicts any cache key not starting with the new VERSION on next visit. (2) Share modal end-to-end: seeded patch via localStorage (patchpot.patches.v1 with version:1/active_id/patches schema, patchpot.patch.<id>.region.v1=London/UK, patchpot.patch.<id>.garden.v1=[{id:'tomato'}]), clicked garden-share-btn → share-patch-create, share minted in ~10s, ALL five required affordances render with EN labels (not raw i18n keys): share-patch-embed-open='Get the embed code', share-patch-qr-download='Download garden-gate QR sticker (PDF)', share-patch-social-kit='Download Social Media Kit (ZIP)', share-patch-tweet='Tweet this patch', share-patch-social-kit-help visible. (3) Social-kit anchor href = https://grow-by-season-1.preview.emergentagent.com/api/share/patch/s2d6xgc6pr9y/social-kit.zip — REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + correct path + .zip suffix. (4) Tweet button: tagName=BUTTON (not A); clicking with stubbed window.open captures URL = https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=...One+plant+is+all+it+takes...%23smallspacegarden&url=https%3A%2F%2F...api%2Fshare%2Fpreview%2Fs2d6xgc6pr9y — contains both 'url=' and 'text=' query params as required. (5) Backend regression: pytest test_story_image_iter35 + test_captions_iter34 + test_social_kit_iter33 → 13/13 PASSED (130s). No regressions from SW version bump.
critical_code_review_comments: sw.js v5 bump is purely cosmetic version-string change at line 5; SHELL_CACHE/RUNTIME_CACHE template-string-derive from VERSION so they automatically become 'patchpot-v5-shell' and 'patchpot-v5-runtime'. activate handler's filter `!k.startsWith(VERSION)` will correctly evict ALL patchpot-v4-* caches on next visit — safe, idempotent.

No functional change to fetch handler — /api/guide-pdf/ still bypassed, /api/* still stale-while-revalidate, same-origin assets still network-first. The user's stale-cache bug will self-resolve when they next load the SPA after redeploy: install fires (skipWaiting), activate fires (clients.claim + evict v4 caches), next /api/share/patch/.../social-kit.zip request fetches from network into the fresh v5 runtime cache.

Preview ingress sets 'cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on /sw.js — good, ensures browsers always re-fetch the SW itself and can detect the version bump without being blocked by HTTP cache.
SharePatchModal.jsx unchanged from iter35; all five affordances + Spanish locale still work as designed.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Critical seed-schema gotcha for /garden share flow on this app: the patches index is {version:1, active_id, patches:[{id,name,created_at}]} NOT {index, active_id, ...}. Garden array items need 'id' field (used in p.id.startsWith('ai-') at MyGarden.jsx:82) — 'plant_id' will crash with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith'). Share button only renders when region is truthy (see MyGarden.jsx:47). Once region+patches+garden are seeded correctly on the origin BEFORE navigating to /garden, the share flow works in ~10-15s (first mint involves AI caption generation). window.open stub MUST be installed via page.add_init_script before navigation. SW endpoint: /sw.js (no /api prefix, served from frontend bundle).
rca_of_the_issue: Production bug ('Only Pinterest shows. Social kit not appearing.') was a stale browser SW/runtime-cache issue, NOT a code bug. Investigation confirmed: (a) prod /api/share/patch/.../social-kit.zip|captions.json|story.png all return 200; (b) prod bundle main.8c90cf32.js DOES contain the share-patch-social-kit/tweet/story testids. Mitigation: bump sw.js VERSION from patchpot-v4 → patchpot-v5 so the activate handler aggressively evicts any v4-* cache on the user's next visit after redeploy. This testing run is regression-only confirmation that the version bump itself is harmless — share modal still renders all five affordances on preview, backend endpoints still pass 13/13 pytest.
